'''Mikhail Vasilyevich Menshikov''' ({{langx|ru|Михаи́л Васи́льевич Ме́ньшиков}}; 17 January 1948 – 1 May 2026<ref>{{Cite web |title=In Memory of Mikhail Menshikov |url=https://www.durham.ac.uk/departments/academic/mathematical-sciences/news/mikhail-menshikov/ |access-date=30 May 2026 |website=Durham University |language=en-gb}}</ref>) was a Russian-British mathematician with publications in areas ranging from [[probability]] to [[combinatorics]]. He held the post of Professor in the [[University of Durham]] until his death in 2026.

Menshikov has made a substantial contribution to [[percolation theory]] and the theory of [[random walks]].{{citation needed|date=October 2019}}

Menshikov was born in [[Moscow]] and went to school in [[Kharkov]], Ukrainian SSR, Soviet Union. He studied at [[Moscow State University]] earning all his degrees up to [[Candidate of Sciences]] (1976) and [[Doctor of Sciences]] (1988). After briefly working in [[Gromov Flight Research Institute|Zhukovsky]], Menshikov worked in Moscow State University for many years. His career then took him to the [[University of São Paulo]] before becoming a professor at the University of Durham.<ref>{{cite web |last=Menshikov |first=Mikhail |title=Professor Mikhail Menshikov – Staff profile |website=Durham University |url=https://www.durham.ac.uk/staff/mikhail-menshikov/ |access-date=11 November 2025}}</ref>
